chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from Zurara, who said:

I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) about an Imam who led a group in prayer, and he remembered that he was not in a state of ablution. So he left, took a man by the hand, brought him forward, and placed him ahead, while the one who was placed ahead did not know what the group had already prayed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pray with them. So if he errs, the group should glorify with him and build upon the prayer of the one who was before him.'

key_terms.سَبَّحَ الْقَوْمُ بِهِ: The group glorified with him (indicating following the leader's error)
key_terms.فَانْصَرَفَ: He left/withdrew (from the state of purity)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the congregational prayer if the Imam realizes he broke his ablution mid-prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* from the prominent narrator Zurarah, this hadith establishes the principle of *al-bina'* (building upon the previous prayer) when an Imam's ablution is broken mid-prayer without his immediate knowledge. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the Imam's continued leadership validates the congregation's prayer, distinguishing it from the Hanafi view of *fard* (obligatory) vs. *nafl* (voluntary) layers, and emphasizes the congregation's role in correcting errors through *tasbih*.
